events.text: The Ghost Market opens only on moonless nights, under a bridge that is not there by day. Jeok Yuhwa, who sells what should not be sold, has kept a stall there for forty years. Tonight she has one thing on her cloth: a pole wrapped in grey silk that moves, slowly, though there is no wind. "The Heaven-Calling Banner," she says. "Raise it, and the sky comes for you before you are ready. Some people find that useful."

effects.log: She counts every coin twice. "It never stays still," she says, handing it over. "Neither will you, now."
"A woman named Seol Mokhwa, three hundred years ago," Jeok Yuhwa says. "She founded a whole sect on surviving it. The sect did not survive her." You leave with the story, and without the banner.
You walk away. Behind you the grey silk turns on its pole, as if it is watching you go.

events.text: A man in a mended scholar's robe stops you on the road with a long bundle under one arm. His family has kept a banner for six generations, he says, and his family has run out of rice. Jeok Yuhwa of the Ghost Market sent him to you: she said you were rich enough, and reckless enough. He unwraps a corner. The silk inside is moving.

choices.text: Buy it and feed his family (6000 taels)

effects.log: He weeps a little, and is ashamed of it. "Do not raise it until you must," he says. "My grandfather did not wait."

choices.text: Give him some silver and leave the banner

effects.log: He stares at the coins, then at the banner, and carries it away still wrapped. You think he is relieved.

choices.text: Tell him you want nothing heaven has to be called for

effects.log: He nods slowly. "That is what my grandfather said," he says, "once."

events.text: In the cloud market, where immortals trade what mortals would die for, a stall keeper with Jeok Yuhwa's sharp face and a thousand more years in it beckons you over. "The same banner," she says. "It came up the stairs after its last owner. Below, it skips a mortal's few years. Here it skips centuries."

effects.log: She takes the stones without counting them. "Heaven hates to be hurried," she says. "That is the whole fun of it."

choices.text: Ask how she came to be here

effects.log: "Everyone who sells what should not be sold ends up here eventually," she says. "So does everyone who buys it."
You leave it. The cloud market is full of things you could buy and should not.

events.text: In the last chamber of the Secret Realm, behind a guardian's empty bed of bones and moss, a pole stands upright in the stone. Grey silk is wrapped around it, and it is moving, slowly, as if something under the cloth is breathing. Carved at its foot: SEOL MOKHWA RAISED ME AND LIVED. WHO IS NEXT.

choices.text: Pull it out of the stone and take it

effects.log: It comes away easily, as if it was waiting. Outside, the realm's sky flickers once.

choices.text: Take it, and swear to raise it only for a good cause

effects.log: You say the oath aloud in the empty chamber. The silk goes still for a moment, as if listening.
You leave it in the stone. Whoever comes next will read the same question.

events.text: The cave's master left a letter with the inheritance: My art you may have. The banner you may not want. I raised it once, at Peak Master, and lived, and spent the rest of my life afraid of the sky. Beside the letter, wrapped in grey silk, a pole moves very slightly in the still air.

choices.text: Take the banner with the art

effects.log: You take both. The letter you keep too, folded inside the silk.
You leave the banner in the cave with its letter. Some inheritances are warnings.

choices.text: Burn the letter and take the banner

effects.log: You burn the letter. A master's fear is not yours to carry, only the banner.

events.text: The old immortal's cave holds nothing but dust and one grey banner leaning against the wall, its silk turning slowly in no wind. A jade slip beside it says: I came up the stairs early, under this. Every century since, the sky has looked at me as a creditor looks at a debtor.

effects.log: It is lighter than it looks. The sky above the clouds seems, for a moment, to notice.

choices.text: Leave it with its owner's dust

effects.log: You leave it. The slip goes on saying what it says to nobody.

events.text: An old man with a straight back and a crooked staff is waiting at your gate before dawn. Gu Haesol, he says, last keeper of the Banner Sect, which has had no other members for ninety years. He does not ask for the banner back. He asks only to see it. When you unwrap it he touches the silk once, the way one touches the cheek of someone sleeping.

effects.log: "She raised it at First-Rate," Gu Haesol says, "and the sky tried for three days to kill her. Then it gave up, and she laughed. That laugh is the whole sect, really."

choices.text: Promise him you will raise it only when you are ready

effects.log: "Nobody is ever ready," he says. "But it is a kind promise. I will hold you to it."
He shakes his head. "It went looking for you," he says. "A keeper keeps. He does not choose."

events.text: Gu Haesol comes back, older, to hear how it went. You tell him: the banner raised, the storm called years early, and you on your feet at the end of it. He sits down on your step and laughs, exactly as you imagine Seol Mokhwa laughed. "There," he says. "The sect is not dead after all."

effects.log: The two of you laugh until the servants come out to see. It feels like a funeral and a festival at once.

choices.text: Ask him to write it down

effects.log: He writes it on the last page of the Banner Sect's book, in a hand that shakes only a little.

events.text: Gu Haesol comes back, older, and you tell him the truth: you raised the banner, and the storm won, and the banner burned down to its pole in your hands. He listens without a word. Then he takes the blackened pole from you and holds it like a walking stick. "Seol Mokhwa lost twice before she won," he says. "Nobody remembers that part."

choices.text: Ask him to stay a while

effects.log: He stays the winter. He teaches you a breathing he says is the Banner Sect's, and is not sure it is.
"Sorry is for things you did not mean," he says. "You meant it. Good."

events.text: The banner's storm is gone. Where it stood there is a black ring burned into the mountain, and in the middle of it you, still standing, with ash in your hair and a realm you were not meant to reach for {tbn_skip}. Somewhere far away, people who felt the sky shake are already asking whose name to say.

effects.log: You say your name to the empty sky, plainly. It does not answer. It does not need to.
You bow to the sky you defied. Defiance and courtesy, the old masters said, are the same muscle.

choices.text: Sit down in the ash and breathe

effects.log: You sit in the ash until your heart is quiet. The new realm settles around you like snow.

events.text: The banner burns down to its pole in your hands. The storm does not end so much as lose interest, the way a cat loses interest in something it has already broken. You are alive. Your meridians are twisted like wet rope, and the gate is exactly where it was.

effects.log: You keep the pole. It is only wood now. It is the most honest thing you own.
You throw it as far as you can. The wind carries it farther than you threw it.
You laugh, and it hurts, and you laugh again. Heaven was not ready to be hurried. Neither, it seems, were you.

events.text: A storyteller in a wineshop tells the tale of a cultivator who raised the Heaven-Calling Banner and called the storm years early, and lived. The listeners shout the ending before it comes. You find you know it too, and you know parts the storyteller has left out.

choices.text: Tell the storyteller the missing part

effects.log: The storyteller writes it down at once. By next year every wineshop tells it your way.

choices.text: Keep the missing part to yourself

effects.log: You drink your tea. Some things are only yours, even across lives.

events.text: A teller in an isle wine house spins the tale of one who raised the Heaven-Calling Banner and called the tribulation down years early, and lived. The immortals shout the ending before it comes. So could you, and you know parts the teller left out.

choices.text: Tell the storyteller the missing part

effects.log: The storyteller writes it down at once. By next year every wineshop tells it your way.

choices.text: Keep the missing part to yourself

effects.log: You drink your tea. Some things are only yours, even across lives.

events.text: You dream of a grey banner burning in your hands, and of a sky that simply waited. You wake with your palms stinging. In this life you have never held a banner. Your hands, it seems, remember another.

effects.log: Whatever it was, this life will wait for its gates. The stinging fades by noon.
Seol Mokhwa lost twice before she won. You do not know how you know that.

events.text: In a meditation above the clouds you see a grey banner burning in your hands, and a sky that only waited. You come out with your palms stinging. In this life you have never held a banner. Your hands remember one anyway.

effects.log: Whatever it was, this life will wait for its gates. The stinging fades by noon.
Seol Mokhwa lost twice before she won. You do not know how you know that.
